decks.name: Dinkum Dictionary
decks.tagline: Real Aussie slang nobody under 40 actually knows. Make up a meaning. Fool the room.

cards.answer: A type of carpet shark that lies flat on the seafloor and looks like a shaggy doormat.
A mythical creature said to lurk in swamps, billabongs and creeks, used to scare kids off the water.
A minor car accident — a prang, a fender bender.
Unsteady, crooked or not working properly.
A blowfly — the big noisy ones that hang around the toilet.
To die, or for a machine to stop working completely.
A left-handed person.
Fine red outback dust, or alternatively, complete and utter nonsense.
A rumour or false story — named after the Furphy water carts soldiers gossiped around.
A mischievous, cheeky person who loves a prank and disrespects authority.
An angry mouthful of abuse, as in 'he gave the umpire a gobful'.
A hopeless idiot — named after a famously useless 1920s racehorse.
Of poor or fake quality; dodgy and badly made.
A coward; someone who is pathetically timid.
Completely full, packed to capacity — short for 'chock-a-block'.
Extremely drunk.
An egg — as in 'full as a goog', meaning very drunk or very full.
Tracksuit pants; comfy daggy sweatpants.
Hard work or physical labour.
To start eating enthusiastically; dig into your food.

decks.name: Is That A Real Town?
decks.tagline: These are all genuine Australian place names. Invent why the town is famous. Real fact wins.

cards.answer: A tiny farming locality in northern Victoria; the name likely comes from an Aboriginal word, possibly meaning 'place of the tadpoles'.
A Top End town near Darwin known for its giant fibreglass Boxing Crocodile statue.
A mining town considered the birthplace of Australia's steel industry, named for its iron-ore hills.
A peak in the Alpine National Park, near 'Terrible Hollow' and 'The Crosscut Saw', named by a frustrated cattleman.
A small village whose name records that the land was acquired unexpectedly, 'by chance'.
A rural locality near Sheffield in Tasmania; the road literally goes nowhere else.
A major regional city whose Wiradjuri name is said to mean 'place of many crows'.
A town named not after the fruit but after a dun-coloured bullock called 'Banana'.
A remote salt-mining settlement on Shark Bay, named from the French 'Havre Inutile' (useless harbour).
A Wheatbelt town whose name is thought to mean 'place of the wood used for making spears'.
A small farming village near Albury, famous for organising massive 'Hay Runs' to drought-stricken farmers.
A sinkhole and blackwood forest reserve in the state's north-west, once home to a slide attraction.
A locality on the Eyre Peninsula, named for wells dug in the area during the colonial era.
A Perth suburb whose name derives from a nearby swamp, 'Lake Innaloo', not the toilet.
A small coastal holiday town on the Yorke Peninsula, named by an unimpressed early surveyor.
A bay in southern Tasmania reportedly named after the yellow-and-red wildflowers growing there.

decks.name: After Dark (18+)
decks.tagline: Filthy obscure words and the actual definitions. Lean in. Toggle off if Nan's playing.

cards.answer: The rumbling, gurgling noise made by gas moving through your guts.
The act of stretching and yawning at the same time, especially when you wake up.
Excessively fond of, or devoted to, one's husband.
An old warning cry shouted before throwing slops and chamber-pot contents out a window.
To dawdle, waste time, or mess about instead of getting on with it.
A wooden puppet on strings; figuratively, a politician controlled by someone else.
A real running training method alternating fast and slow bursts — Swedish for 'speed play'.
A boastful little man with an inflated opinion of himself.
To confuse, fluster or bewilder someone completely.
To feel queasy, or for your stomach to roll with nausea.
A shrewd, unprincipled person, especially a scheming politician.
A person who stubbornly clings to a belief or habit even after being proven wrong.
A filthy, slobbering, worthless slob of a person.
The sick, hungover feeling caused by too much eating or drinking.
The mouthpiece block of a recorder or whistle that splits the air.
Relating to the day before yesterday.
